name: world-history-dates

description.en: 87 landmark events of world history, from the Battle of Marathon to the September 11 attacks, spread across eras and continents. The front names the event in English and Swedish; the back gives the year it happened. A plain number is a year AD; years before Christ are written “490 BC” (“490 f.Kr.”). Years from Wikidata, each checked against Store norske leksikon.
description.sv: 87 avgörande händelser i världshistorien, från slaget vid Marathon till 11 september-attackerna, spridda över epoker och världsdelar. Framsidan namnger händelsen på engelska och svenska; baksidan ger året då den inträffade. Ett tal utan tillägg är ett år efter Kristus; år före Kristus skrivs ”490 f.Kr.” (”490 BC”). Årtalen kommer från Wikidata och är kontrollerade mot Store norske leksikon.

method: Who did the work: the research, drafting and cross-checking of this deck were done by AI agents (Claude, Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction on 4 October 2026, using the Wikidata Query Service, the Wikidata API and the Store norske leksikon (SNL) API, with the builder's machine checks against live Wikidata. Review by independent AI reviewers is part of the library's process and is logged under quality control; no human subject expert has reviewed the cards yet.

Candidates: from its own general knowledge, the authoring agent drew up, in five batches, about 250 search strings for widely taught events of world history (some events were searched more than once), deliberately including Africa, the Americas, Asia and Oceania as well as Europe and covering antiquity to the 21st century. No published list or timeline was copied. Each candidate was looked up with the Wikidata wbsearchentities API (English search, four hits; the exact requests are under Queries) and the right item picked by hand from the hits and their descriptions. Four titles that the search did not find were resolved to item ids through the English Wikipedia pageprops API (only the wikibase_item ids were used).

Dates and labels: two SPARQL queries against https://query.wikidata.org/sparql (under Queries) returned, for every candidate item, its English and Swedish labels, Swedish aliases (first query), English and Swedish Wikipedia sitelinks, and the values of P585 point in time, P580 start time, P582 end time, P571 inception, P577 publication date, P619 launch date, P1619 date of official opening and P576 dissolution date. The raw JSON responses were saved and read item by item. One further query fetched the inception (P571) of Australia (Q408).

Choosing the year: for each card the property that dates exactly the event on the front was chosen (for instance P582 end time of the siege of Constantinople for its fall, P580 start time of the Korean War for its outbreak, P1619 official opening of the Suez Canal, P619 launch of Vostok 1 for the first human in space). The card's evidence names the property and its value. Where an item had several conflicting dates, the one matching the card was used and the discrepancy recorded in quality control.

Years before Christ: the Wikidata Query Service writes dates in the XSD 1.1 form, in which 1 BCE is year 0 (https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikibase/Indexing/RDF_Dump_Format: “The xsd:dateTime dates follow XSD 1.1 standard, which uses the proleptic Gregorian calendar, and represents the year 1 BCE as +0000.”). A Query Service year of -489 is therefore 490 BC. The cards give the traditional year (490 BC); their machine checks use the Query Service form (-489). The same page explains why some dates appear shifted by a few days (Julian dates converted to the proleptic Gregorian calendar, e.g. 25 December 800 shown as 800-12-29); for no card does this change the year.

Wording: every front is the deck's own short wording of the event, in English and in Swedish. Where a front uses an item's Wikidata label verbatim (English or Swedish), a label check is attached so the build confirms it. Swedish text not taken from an event's label was written by the authoring agent in Swedish conventions (sentence case; lower-case names of peoples and adjectives). In the first draft the Swedish names of people and places inside such text were written from the agent's knowledge; the Swedish labels or aliases of related items were checked only where a name seemed uncertain (Q408 alias “Australiska statsförbundet”, Q33296 “Mogulriket”). In quality-control round 2 every such name was checked against Wikidata's sv labels and aliases and, where needed, Swedish Wikipedia (queries under Queries): Odovakar (sv label of Q103333; the draft's “Odoaker” was corrected), Qin Shi Huangdi (sv label of Q7192; corrected from “Qin Shi Huang”), Alarik (Q102371 sv label “Alarik I”), Johan utan land (sv alias of Q129308), Karl den store (Q3044), Konstantinopel (Q16869), Mecka (title of the Swedish Wikipedia article on Q5806, whose sv label is the variant “Mekka”), Jurij Gagarin (Q7327), Dagen D (redirect on Swedish Wikipedia to “Landstigningen i Normandie”, whose lead names 6 June 1944 “Dagen D”). Short frontNotes disambiguate battles that share a name with other battles; backNotes explain conventions (the Julian date of the October Revolution, AD years below 100, the Hijra as year 1 of the Islamic calendar).

Back convention: years AD are untagged numbers (“1789”); years before Christ are tagged text, “490 BC” in English and “490 f.Kr.” in Swedish. AD 9 and AD 79 carry a backNote saying AD so they are not mistaken for an unmarked BC year.

Independent check: every card's year was checked against Store norske leksikon, the Norwegian national encyclopedia, whose articles are written and signed by subject experts. For each card the SNL search API (https://snl.no/api/v1/search) was queried, the article JSON of the top hits fetched (https://snl.no/<article>.json) and its sentences containing the year read; where the first search found nothing, further searches were run (all listed under Queries). The verbatim sentence, with an English gloss, is in each card's evidence. Before SNL, a few Encyclopaedia Britannica, encyclopedia.com and infoplease article URLs were requested as a possible independent check; the exact URLs were not recorded. Britannica refused the automated requests (HTTP 403) and the other two returned not-found, so none of them returned content and none was used. The Battle of Talas (751) was dropped because no SNL article stating its year was found.

Build and validation: the dossier was built with python3 packages/deck-library/scripts/authored_decks.py build world-history-dates, which re-ran every Wikidata check (the date of every card, plus the labels used) against live Wikidata, and the deck was validated with node packages/deck-library/scripts/validate_sources.ts world-history-dates (the app's SHACL shapes and DCAT-AP).

Notes and quality control: after the independent reviews, every frontNote and backNote was compared with the card's evidence, and where a note stated a fact its evidence did not contain, either a supporting SNL sentence or Wikidata statement was added to the evidence or the note was cut back to what the evidence says (logged in quality-control round 3). The SNL articles were re-fetched as https://snl.no/<article>.json and searched for sentences supporting each note; the Wikidata statements were fetched with the queries listed under Queries.
selection: Included: landmark events that are widely taught in world history, that happened in a single year that the sources agree on, and that can be named unambiguously in a short phrase. Processes and wars are only included through a single dated moment (a war breaking out, a city falling, a treaty being signed, a revolution beginning), and the front says which moment is meant. The set is spread across eras (antiquity to 2001) and continents (Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania), with a few events of special interest to Swedish learners (the Kalmar Union, the Stockholm Bloodbath, Poltava). Left out because the year is disputed or not a single year: the Battle of Tours (732 or 733), the Battle of Kadesh (the Egyptian chronologies differ), the founding of Rome (legendary), the East–West Schism (a process conventionally dated 1054), the Glorious Revolution (1688–1689), the Black Death (1346–1353), Gutenberg's first printing (uncertain), the Iranian Revolution (1978–1979). Left out because Wikidata's date conflicts with the commonly given one and the deck takes its dates from Wikidata: the Convention of Kanagawa (Wikidata 1864, commonly 1854) and the Suez Crisis (point in time 1957 alongside a 1956 start). Left out for lack of an independent check: the Battle of Talas (751). Further candidates were left out only to keep the deck near 80 cards and balanced between regions (among them Salamis, Zama, Trafalgar, Austerlitz, Lützen, the Wall Street Crash, the Salt March and the Bandung Conference).

The SNL sentences in the provenance report are short quotations made under SNL's quotation allowance; each is attributed by the article's URL, where the article's named authors and its licence (fri gjenbruk CC BY-SA 3.0 or begrenset gjenbruk) are shown. Treating every article under the stricter begrenset terms is also safe for the articles marked fri.

rounds.lens: Machine checks against live Wikidata and a card-by-card cross-check of every year against Store norske leksikon
rounds.summary: The builder's Wikidata checks cover every card: the property value that dates the card's event (P585, P580, P582, P571, P577, P619 or P1619), plus the English and Swedish Wikidata labels wherever a front uses one verbatim, and two Swedish aliases of related items. Every year was confirmed by a sentence in Store norske leksikon. The findings below record where the two sources' dates differ in day or framing (in no case in the year), how the card was framed to stay unambiguous, and the candidates that were dropped.

findings.issue: The Wikidata Query Service gives BCE years in XSD 1.1 numbering (1 BCE = year 0), e.g. -0489 for the Battle of Marathon.
findings.resolution: Cards show the traditional year (490 BC); the checks expect the Query Service form (-489). The convention is quoted from the Wikibase RDF format documentation in the method.

findings.issue: Wikidata has P585 28 June 1919 (signing) and P580 10 January 1920 (entry into force; SNL says 20 January 1920).
findings.resolution: The front says the treaty is signed; the year 1919 is checked against P585 and confirmed by SNL.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P585 is 15 March 1991 (not the reunification day), while P582 end time is 3 October 1990, which SNL confirms.
findings.resolution: Card year 1990, checked against P582. P585 is not used.

findings.issue: Wikidata's start time is 10 May 1857 (Meerut); SNL dates the beginning to the end of March 1857 (Mangal Pandey). The name “Indian Rebellion of 1857” would give the answer away.
findings.resolution: Same year in both. The front says the rebellion breaks out and uses the name Sepoy Rebellion / Sepoyupproret.

findings.issue: Wikidata start time 7 April 1994; SNL says the killing began on 6 April 1994.
findings.resolution: Same year; no change.

findings.issue: Wikidata P577 is 10 November 1517 (proleptic Gregorian); SNL gives 31 October 1517.
findings.resolution: Same year; no change.

findings.issue: Wikidata gives 1498 (year precision). The SNL sentence gives 18 May without the year, which follows from the article's narrative (left Lisbon 8 July 1497, reached the African coast 4 November 1497).
findings.resolution: Kept; the evidence quotes both sentences and explains the inference.

findings.issue: SNL's sentence “angrep Polen 1. september” takes its year from the surrounding 1939 narrative.
findings.resolution: Kept; the evidence quotes the surrounding sentences. Wikidata P580 is 1 September 1939.

findings.issue: SNL says Atahualpa was captured “later the same year” after a sentence dated 1532.
findings.resolution: Kept; both sentences are quoted. Wikidata P585 for the Battle of Cajamarca is 1532.

findings.issue: The Wikidata item is the Algerian War, whose end time (1962-09-09) is not independence day.
findings.resolution: Only the year is used; SNL states that Algeria became independent in 1962.

findings.issue: Wikidata's date for Apollo 11 is the launch (16 July 1969), not the landing.
findings.resolution: Same year; SNL gives the landing as 20 July 1969.

findings.issue: SNL says the union formally existed 1389/1397–1521 (Wikidata's dissolution is 1523).
findings.resolution: The card asks only for the formation, which both date to 1397 (SNL: Eric crowned in Kalmar in 1397, “and so the Kalmar Union was founded”).

findings.issue: Wikidata has two P585 values (October and November 79), reflecting the debate about the day.
findings.resolution: The year 79 is undisputed. A backNote says AD 79.

findings.issue: The revolution is dated 25 October (Julian) or 7 November (Gregorian) 1917.
findings.resolution: Same year; a backNote explains the name.

findings.issue: The revolution broke out in 1911 but the Republic of China was proclaimed in 1912 (Wikidata end time 12 February 1912).
findings.resolution: The front asks when it breaks out (P580, 1911); a backNote gives the 1912 proclamation.

findings.issue: A first draft of the front (“open to citizens of all races”) was clumsy, especially in Swedish.
findings.resolution: Reworded as the first election with universal suffrage, following the Wikidata description of Q957012.

findings.issue: No SNL article stating the year 751 for the battle was found (searches listed under Queries).
findings.resolution: Card removed.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P585 for Q771451 is 1864-03-31, while the treaty is commonly dated 1854 (not researched further).
findings.resolution: Left out rather than taking the year from a verification source or contradicting the content source.

findings.issue: Wikidata has P585 1957-03-01 alongside start time 29 October 1956.
findings.resolution: Left out.

findings.issue: For these four cards the Wikidata check confirms only the year, not the exact moment on the front: Q3771259 P580 is the departure of Columbus's first voyage (1492-08-12, landfall 12 October), Q43653 P619 the launch of Apollo 11 (16 July 1969, landing 20 July), Q200790 P582 the end of the Algerian War (1962-09-09, not independence day), Q2986801 P582 the end of Qin's wars of unification. (Added after QC round 1.)
findings.resolution: Each event falls in the same year as the property checked, and SNL confirms the year of the event on the front. The checks are year checks only and would not catch a mismatch between front and date within that year.

findings.issue: Wikidata Q87779 contradicts itself: P585 is 0009-09-01 (AD 9), but its English description says “9 BCE”. (Added after QC round 3.)
findings.resolution: The card follows P585 and SNL (Osnabrück and Arminius articles: “år 9 evt.”), and the discrepancy is noted in the card's evidence.

rounds.scope: All 87 cards: every year compared with the English Wikipedia lead of the card's Wikidata item, the builder's Wikidata checks re-run, notes and description read

One warning (the Abbasid Caliphate did not strictly end in 1258) was fixed by rewording the front and adding a sourced backNote; the Hong Kong Island precision was fixed; two frontNote suggestions were already met by the cards; the year-only Wikidata checks are now listed in round 0.

findings.resolution: Verified in SNL (kalifat: the Mamluk sultans took a claimed relative of the last caliph to Cairo; in 1517 the Ottomans took the last of these “shadow caliphs” to Istanbul). The front now says “The Mongols sack Baghdad and kill the Abbasid caliph” / “Mongolerna intar Bagdad och dödar den abbasidiske kalifen” (SNL abbasidane: the Mongols burned Baghdad and killed the caliph and his family in 1258), with a backNote “Conventionally the end of the Abbasid Caliphate; powerless Abbasid caliphs lived on in Cairo until 1517”. Evidence from SNL abbasidane and kalifat added, plus a check of Q12536 P576 = 1258.

findings.issue: Suggested a frontNote to tell the 480 BC battle from those of 279 and 191 BC.
findings.resolution: The card already has that frontNote: “Leonidas and the Spartans against the Persians of Xerxes” / “Leonidas och spartanerna mot Xerxes perser”, supported by SNL Thermopylai.

findings.issue: Suggested a frontNote to tell the 1571 battle from the 1499 one.
findings.resolution: The card already has exactly the suggested frontNote: “The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet” / “Heliga ligan besegrar den osmanska flottan”.

findings.resolution: Confirmed by the card's own SNL quote (“avstå øya Hongkong”). frontNote now “Ends the First Opium War; China cedes Hong Kong Island to Britain” / “Avslutar första opiumkriget; Kina avträder ön Hongkong till Storbritannien”, and the gloss of the SNL quote now says “the island of Hong Kong”.

findings.issue: Four Wikidata checks confirm only the year, not the dated event on the front (Columbus departure, Apollo 11 launch, end of the Algerian War, end of Qin's wars of unification).
findings.resolution: Verified against the evidence. The cards are right; a round 0 finding now lists all four as year-only checks.

findings.resolution: The capitalisation was wrong (Q83164 sv label confirmed). findings.resolution: Verified (Q7192 sv label “Qin Shi Huangdi”; the sv.wikipedia article has the same title). The sv front now uses “Qin Shi Huangdi”, and sv and en label checks on Q7192 were added (the English front keeps the en label “Qin Shi Huang”).

findings.resolution: Now “The Islamic calendar counts its years from it” / “Den islamiska tideräkningen räknas från den”.

findings.resolution: The backNote is now “Often regarded as the start of the French Revolution” / “Räknas ofta som början på franska revolutionen”. The hedge follows the SNL sentence now quoted in the evidence (“Angrepet blir ofte regnet som starten på den franske revolusjon”).

findings.resolution: The frontNote now names China as the subject: “Avslutar första opiumkriget; Kina avträder ön Hongkong till Storbritannien” (English likewise; see round 1).

findings.issue: The English front names the victims (“Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda”), the Swedish front does not (“Folkmordet i Rwanda”).
findings.resolution: Declined. Each front uses the established name in its language: the English follows the Wikidata en label (“1994 Genocide against Tutsi”, the UN's term) without the year, and the Swedish is the Wikidata sv label checked by the build (SNL likewise writes “Folkemordet i Rwanda”). Both name the same event unambiguously, and the card asks only for its year.

rounds.reviewer: Claude (AI) — independent Licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer
rounds.scope: All 87 cards' evidence (every SNL quote and Wikidata value re-fetched), sources, licence evidence, method, queries and licensing
rounds.summary: The licensing was sound. The documentation gaps were fixed: the unrecorded Britannica, encyclopedia.com and infoplease requests are now described honestly; the Xinhai backNote has evidence; every frontNote and backNote in the deck (not only the reviewer's examples) was compared with its evidence, so supporting sentences were added or the notes were cut back; the Teutoburg discrepancy and the stray ids are documented; and SNL attribution is stated.

findings.resolution: Evidence added: Wikidata Q13426199 (Republic of China 1912–1949) P571 = 1912-01-01 at day precision (timePrecision 11, queried), with a check, and SNL Kinas_historie (“Revolusjonen i 1911 førte til opprettelsen av Republikken Kina i 1912”). findings.issue: Several notes stated facts that no evidence supports (Mandela becomes president, three legions at Teutoburg, Mughal founding at Panipat, Marathon as the first Persian invasion, Plassey/East India Company/Bengal).
findings.resolution: Confirmed, and the check was widened to all 32 notes [corrected in round 4: the deck has 33 frontNote/backNote entries; the count was wrong, no note was added after the check]. Evidence added where sources support the note: Mandela (SNL: “Mandela vart det demokratiske Sør-Afrikas første president”; Wikidata Q8023 P39 President of South Africa from 1994-05-10), Panipat (SNL Babur “grunnleggeren av moguldynastiet”; Wikidata Q33296 P571 = 1526, checked), Cannae (SNL: Hannibal defeated the Romans), Westphalia (SNL: the parties of the Thirty Years' War; Wikidata description “peace treaty ending the Thirty and Eighty Years' Wars”), Poltava (SNL: Tsar Peter I; Charles XII fled), Waterloo (SNL: “Napoleons definitive nederlag”), Carthage (SNL: the Third Punic War 149–146 BCE), Bastille (SNL: often regarded as the start of the Revolution). findings.resolution: Verified live. Logged in round 0 and noted in the card's Wikidata evidence. Wikidata itself was not edited.

findings.issue: The Swedish-alias lookup included stray ids, and the method did not say that the non-label Swedish names were unchecked.
findings.resolution: The query's purpose now names the relevant ids and the stray ones. Q7186 does return an entity (Marie Curie, which has descriptions but no en/sv labels in that response), but it is stray all the same. All the non-label Swedish names were then checked against Wikidata sv labels and aliases and Swedish Wikipedia (queries recorded; Swedish Wikipedia added as a verification source). This led to two corrections, Odovakar and Qin Shi Huangdi; the method lists the result for each name.

findings.issue: SNL attribution: the report quotes about 90 SNL sentences while naming the authors only collectively.
findings.resolution: Partly applied. The licensing now states that the quotes are short quotations under SNL's quotation allowance (quoted in licenseEvidence), each attributed by its article URL, where the named authors and the article's licence are shown. Names were not added to every quote: the URL identifies the authored article, and the quotation allowance is satisfied by naming the source.
